subject: Engagement launchpad — hands-on session agenda & prework
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmeinc.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Acme POC Team <acme-poc@acmeinc.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — timing and what we want to cover

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. We'd like to lock in the POC kickoff and a hands-on working session next week if possible. High-level asks:
- 2 hour hands-on workshop with prompt review and routing workshop (we'll bring a few real prompts)
- short load test window afterwards (30–45 minutes) to validate throughput assumptions
- a short one-page SOW or checklist so legal/procurement can see the scope

Preferred slots: Sep 10 morning (PST) or Sep 11 afternoon (PST). Our core attendees will be Tom Harris (platform lead), Priya S., and one data engineer.

I've attached our short requirements note. Can you confirm availability and what you need from us ahead of time?

Thanks,
Tom

Attachment: acme-poc-requirements.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Acme POC Team <acme-poc@acmeinc.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — timing and what we want to cover

Tom —

Great, thanks for the note and the requirements doc. We can support a 2-hour hands-on session plus a 30–45 minute load validation. Proposed schedule windows (PST):
- Option A: Sep 10, 09:00–11:00 (workshop) + 11:15–11:45 (load test)
- Option B: Sep 11, 13:00–15:00 (workshop) + 15:15–15:45 (load test)

To make the session high-value, please:
- Share 3 representative prompts (anonymized OK) and one sample dataset or context length we should test
- Confirm the list of attendees and whether anyone needs SSO access to our staging console

I'll circulate a short pre-read and a working-session agenda later today. Internally, I'll loop in the engineers to validate capacity.

Are either of those slots good?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_poc_pre-read.pdf (stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC kickoff — timing and what we want to cover

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Quick alignment:
- Owner: Neha (facilitation + agenda)
- Dev: handle prompt review, routing policy demo, KV/cache behavior, and confirm model variant matrix for the session
- Dylan: plan the 30–45m load validation; we should reserve a warmup window and have metrics dashboard links ready
- Marissa: coordinate SOW/checklist for procurement and own participant invites

Internal checklist (short):
- Confirm attachment for attendees + SSO provisioning by Sep 8 EOD
- Prepare a 12–15 slide working deck (agenda, prompts, expected outcomes, fallbacks) — Neha will draft slides
- Dev to produce a short runbook for the load test including target TPS, sample payload size, and expected latency SLOs
- Dylan to stub a simple load plan (staggered ramp, peak 2–3 minutes, cool-down) and attach config

Can you confirm availability for either slot? If both are tight, we can propose Sep 12 as a backup.

Thanks — Neha

On Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 09:12 Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmeinc.com> wrote:
> Hi Neha,
> 
> Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. We'd like to lock in the POC kickoff and a hands-on working session next week if possible....

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC kickoff — timing and what we want to cover

All — I'm available for both proposed slots but leaning toward Sep 10 morning to keep momentum. Technical notes for planning:
- Prompt review: request the 3 prompts by Sep 8 so we can pre-run in a sandbox; please indicate desired decoding settings (top_p/temperature) if specific
- Routing demo: I'll prepare two routing policies to show: (1) latency-priority -> low-quant model variant, (2) cost-priority -> batched quantized variant. Need sample sequence length distribution from Acme
- KV/prefix caching: bring a short example to demonstrate cache hit/miss and expected token savings
- Model matrix: suggest we demo gpt-open-13b-q4 and gpt-open-70b-q8 (or equivalents) so we can show perf/cost tradeoffs

Load plan (high level):
- Warmup: 3 minutes at 20% traffic
- Ramp: 5 minutes to target TPS (we need to agree target; 100 TPS recommended for a light validation)
- Peak: 3 minutes at target
- Cooldown: 4 minutes back to baseline

I'll attach a stub load config (YAML) and a one-page tech checklist. If we have permission to run higher throughput we can scale, but need confirmation of the capacity commitment for the window.

Attachments: loadtest_plan_stub.yml, tech_checklist_onepage.pdf

— Dev
